rendered: The starting point is the total known global cobalt reserves, taken from the United States Geological Survey 2021 report on cobalt[1]: 7 million metric tons[2]. The review then applies a mining-efficiency factor and a battery-share factor. The mining efficiency is a conservative yearly figure of ≈70%[3], and the share of mined cobalt directed toward battery manufacturing is ≈40%[4]. Applying these to the reserves gives the cobalt available for battery industries, ≈2 million metric tons globally[5]. The review calls this the usable battery-specific cobalt from the total reserves, and gives only these endpoints and factors, not the intermediate arithmetic. This usable amount underlies its conclusion that demand will exceed the reserves available for battery manufacturing before 2045 (Figure 1c)[6].
